title: 2006 HMMT February Guts Problem 7
statement:
Find all real numbers \(x\) such that

\[x^{2}+\left\lfloor\frac{x}{2}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{x}{3}\right\rfloor=10\]

solutions.text: Evidently \(x^{2}\) must be an integer. Well, there aren't that many things to check, are there? Among positive \(x, \sqrt{8}\) is too small and \(\sqrt{9}\) is too big; among negative \(\mathrm{x},-\sqrt{15}\) is too small and \(-\sqrt{13}\) is too big.
